title: Eigenfaces: Linear Algebra Learns to Recognize Faces (1991)
explainer: In 1991, Matthew Turk and Alex Pentland showed that treating each face image as a long vector and computing the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of a set of face images produces a small set of 'eigenfaces' that can reconstruct and distinguish faces using far fewer numbers than the raw pixels. It was one of the first widely cited demonstrations that eigendecomposition, the same linear-algebra operation underlying principal component analysis, could do real feature learning on messy, high-dimensional real-world data rather than just textbook matrices. Eigenfaces is a direct ancestor of the matrix-factorization and dimensionality-reduction techniques still used throughout ML to turn raw data into learnable vector representations.
